messages.subject: generalizing R-hat to ragged arrays
parts:
R-hat involves a couple of averages over chains.
My question is whether I should make those weighted
by the size of the chain or not.

I've attached a PDF.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] generalizing R-hat to ragged arrays
parts:
Hi, Bob. In a multilevel modeling context the weights would be a compromise (of course) between weighting the chains equally and weighting proportional to sample size. But here we want a reasonable hack, I think. My intuition is that equal weighting is safest.
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] generalizing R-hat to ragged arrays
parts:
On 5/22/12 8:56 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> Hi, Bob. In a multilevel modeling context the weights would be a compromise (of course) between weighting
> the chains equally and weighting proportional to sample size.

> But here we want a reasonable hack, I think.
That, or it's Stan models all the way down.
> My intuition is that equal weighting is safest.

That's what it felt like to me, too.
I was worried that weighting by size would
let one long chain dominate a bunch of shorter
ones, which isn't what we want in a diagnostic.

OK -- your turn to think of something to talk
about at the Stan meeting :-)

We can talk about the IES grant afterward. I'd like
to find some good motivating categorical models.
Especially ones where it's not easy or practical to sum
out the categorical parameters.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] generalizing R-hat to ragged arrays
parts:
I'm happy to talk to them and/or send the manual.

The LaTeX for the manual's online and when we do
the release, we'll release v 1.0 of the manual, too.

In writing the log posterior, they need to be
able to do it with just the functions we provide
or functions they write in terms of ones we provide,
which are documented in the manual. That means
no Bessel functions or other such shenanigans!

- Bob
